narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: Today on The Daily Rundown: where AI spending goes, and whether agents could replace your apps.

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: Then, the trust behind secure devices—and why bond-market fine print matters in a crisis.

narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: On All-In, the hosts preview Ramp spending data, separating GPU compute from payments to closed-model labs. With open-weight models competing, that split helps explain who's paying to run AI themselves.

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: On the a16z Podcast, Ben Horowitz considers software that's cheap to clone and agents that could replace applications. For founders, the stakes are concrete: what makes an AI business defensible?

narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: On Oxide and Friends, the crew explains public key infrastructure—the trust system behind secure device provisioning—and its operational costs. With iPhone and Samsung TV hacks in today's headlines, that foundation matters.

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: On Masters in Business, journalist Robin Wigglesworth recalls advising a colleague covering a crisis, before a discussion of debt, Islamic bonds, and documentation. For investors, the fine print can become the story.

narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: That's The Daily Rundown. Thanks for listening.
